ai_show_review.summary: High‑energy Pigpen blues set with fiery Smokestack Lightning and soaring Viola Lee
ai_show_review.blurb: The flatbed‑truck gig delivers a blistering blues marathon highlighted by Viola Lee Blues, Smokestack Lightning and Turn On Your Lovelight. Jerry’s lead work is hypnotic while Pigpen dominates vocals and organ. A solid, high‑octane performance captured on a listenable audience tape.
ai_show_review.review: The March 3 1968 Haight Street flatbed‑truck free concert finds the Dead in full blues mode, riding a wave of raw crowd enthusiasm. From the opening howl of Viola Lee Blues, Garcia spins a hypnotic solo that sets the tone for a set packed with Pigpen‑fronted firepower – his gritty organ swells and commanding vocals blaze through Smokestack Lightning and Turn On Your Lovelight. Phil’s bass weaves a magical undercurrent that keeps the jams grounded, while Bob adds a memorable final verse on Lovelight. The middle of the show veers into experimental territory with the classic Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One sandwich before closing on a spirited Dancin' In The Street. Though captured on mono audience tape, the recording is surprisingly clear for its era and presents the full set without major gaps, making it the go‑to source for this historic early‑68 performance.

best_recording.reason: Fair‑quality mono audience tape with the most complete set and fewer dropouts than other sources

key_highlights: Hypnotic Viola Lee Blues solo that showcases Garcia’s early improvisational flair
Fiery Smokestack Lightning driven by Pigpen’s powerhouse vocals and organ
Magical Phil Lesh bass line that anchors the high‑octane blues jams
Rare early sandwich: Cryptical Envelopment → The Other One → Cryptical Envelopment

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a hypnotic solo on Viola Lee Blues and a searing lead during Smokestack Lightning, while keeping solid rhythm throughout the set.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a magical, melodic bass line that underpins the high‑octane blues jams, especially evident in the extended Smokestack Lightning.
band_performance.Bob: Steps up for the final verse of Turn On Your Lovelight, adding a memorable vocal touch and steady rhythm guitar work.
band_performance.Pigpen: Commands the stage with powerhouse vocals on Smokestack Lightning and Turn On Your Lovelight, plus gritty organ textures that drive the blues‑heavy set.
